profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at Arm, Ltd.
profile.summary:
I'm a software engineer at Arm, focused on open-source networking projects. My current focus is on AI Networking and the role of CCLs in PyTorch based applications. Previously, I've focused on a variety of userspace networking projects. I was the maintainer for Arm's dataplane-stack and cloud-native network function reference architecture (CRA) solutions projects. Dataplane-stack is focused on providing a high-throughput user-space packet processing software stack built on popular OSS projects like DPDK and VPP. CRA was focused on seamless orchestration of userspace networking applications with Kubernetes. Previously to these projects, I  benchmarked the RCU implementation of DPDK vs the implementation within Userspace RCU. RCU is commonly used for safe memory reclamation in lock-free data structures and algorithms. My work was presented in FOSDEM '22!

While at the University of Michigan, I performed research in reducing front-end processor stalls for data-center applications. The work was published as Twig in Micro '21.

My interests lie in AI networking use cases, distributed parallelisms for AI models, how software can best utilize modern hardware features, and rock climbing.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description: I am focused on understanding and optimizing AI Networking use cases for Arm based systems

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
For the first 6 months, I continued my role as maintainer of the CRA and dataplane stack solutions projects.
In June of 2024, I moved full-time onto the AI Networking project, focusing on understanding the role of CCLs in PyTorch-based applications, such as TorchTitan.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: In this role, I maintained Arm's cloud-native network function reference architecture (CRA) and dataplane-stack reference solutions. These projects exposed me to real-world userspace networking use cases, such as SSL reverse proxy and TCP termination, as well as deployment scenarios leveraging on-prem K8s and on AWS. As maintainer, my focus was on combining high quality code contributions from myself and teammates with easy to read documentation and a seamless out of the box experience.

positions.title: Graduate Software Engineer
positions.description: In this role, I benchmarked the RCU implementation within DPDK against the popular alternative- Userspace RCU. RCU is typically utilized for safe memory reclamation in lock-free data structures and algorithms. I presented my work & results at FOSDEM '22. My next project focused on enabling cloud-native deployments of networking functions on the Arm architecture and building reference applications leveraging DPDK & VPP.

positions.title: Graduate Student Instructor
positions.description: As a Graduate Student Instructor for EECS 482: Operating Systems, I lead weekly lab sections with students to work through practice problems and cover lecture material. I host office hours to help students translate the theory behind the lectures to apply them in their projects. I also help create tough but fair exam questions and assist other staff members in preparing for their lab sections. Due to COVID-19, I have worked with other staff to devise community building methods in an all-virtual environment this semester.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: I wrote modern C++ leveraging key concepts such as safe memory management, lockfree data structures, distributed systems protocols, dependency injection for modularity and testability, and template metaprogramming. I applied these skills to testing and debugging their redesigned data loader and expanding their user access controls.

positions.title: Instructional Assistant
positions.description: As an undergraduate instructional assistant for EECS 482: Operating Systems, I led weekly lab sessions where I went over practice problems, reviewed lecture material, and engaged with students to promote understanding. I also hosted weekly office hours where I worked with students  on their projects and helped them translate the theory behind the lectures to the application in their projects. When COVID-19 caused courses to go virtual, I helped the course shift to its new format over  a weekend, and learned new methods to operate effectively in the "new normal."

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description: As a developer tools intern, I added support for User Statically Defined Tracepoints (USDT) to MongoDB and consumed these tracepoints with multiple in-kernel eBPF tools to highly previously inaccessible insights about the database. These insights included which locks were most hotly contended  for, the root cause of different failures,  grouping commands that failed in similar ways, generating histograms based on the latency of commands, and logging queries that took more time than a desired threshold. Additionally, I designed and implemented a multi-process testing framework to thoroughly test the USDT interface.

positions.title: Digital Technology Intern
positions.description: I was a back-end developer for an internal tool for GE businesses. I worked with SQL, Java, and Spring-Boot and provided 4 key deliverables over my internship. The first was integrating our GE product with another GE product. Second, I cleared attributes of different objects coming back from our database based upon user access. Third, I wrote an endpoint that builds out a tree of database information based upon being provided the information of any node. Finally, I enabled admins to have better control over user access.

positions.title: Lead Research and Development Engineer
positions.description: I researched and evaluated different ways for an autonomous boat to locate an underwater sound source and navigate towards it. I led a team of 5 others in the research and application of sound source localization algorithms to this particular area. I have created a MATLAB simulation for testing various alorithms that we develop.

positions.title: Study Group Facilitator
positions.description: I led a group of 15 students in discussion and practice problems around the material covered in the first physics class for engineers. I held weekly meetings where I conveyed challenging concepts in a new way to help each member maximize their understanding of mechanics. In addition, I provided practice problems for the members to work through with each other in a collaborative learning setting.

company.name: University of Michigan Science Learning Center

positions.title: Software Engineer Internship
positions.description: Developed a cross-platform mobile application for commercial real estate investors using React-Native. I started this internship with 0 prior experience in web development, javascript, or mobile app development. Over the course of this internship, I dived into unit testing with Jest and Enzyme, continuous integration with Bamboo, token cycling and validation within Ruby, and performance improvements with React-Native with React-Navigation.

honors.title: ACM Student Research Competition First Place
honors.description: I won first place at the student research competition (SRC) for undergraduates at the International Symposium for Compiler Generation and Optimization (CGO). I presented my work on mitigating front-end processor stalls due to instruction cache misses. I am continuing work on this project under the mentorship of Professor Kasikci and his PhD student Tanvir Khan. You can read more about my research here: https://cse.engin.umich.edu/stories/undergraduate-research-on-speeding-up-data-centers-earns-acm-first-prize
